text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Punjab provincial government has asked the federal government to ban religious parties involved in sectarianism, Punjab Chief Minister Sardar Arif Nakai said.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan asked banks for financial information on their performance over the last 10 years.

- The Sindh government has set up a special medical board to determine within 24 hours whether the wounds suffered by a police officer during the gunbattle with supporters of Murtaza Bhutto were self-inflicted or otherwise.

- A U.S. credit rating agency has put Pakistan under review, in a new blow to Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's government, but some analysts said success in the upcoming talks with the International Monetary Fund might avert a downgrade.
- Stocks drifted lower on news that a U.S. agency was going to downgrade Pakistan's credit rating.
- Bhoja Airlines (Pvt) Ltd operated its first international flight carrying Pakistani passengers from Dubai to Karachi.
- Opposition leader Nawaz Sharif is meeting President Farooq Leghari on Thursday to discuss the economic and political situation.
- The Kabul government said a pilot of the Islamic Taleban militia defected to Kabul on Tuesday in a transport plane carrying seven Pakistani army officers, who shown to reporters.
- Pakistan rejected a U.S. proposal to deploy its military information support team in Pakistan early next month to target drug traffickers.
- The World Bank will hold a three-day privatisation summit in Pakistan for heads of privatisation departments in all member countries of the Organisation of Islamic Conference.
- Around 80 new and re-conditioned vehicles imported from the United Arab Emirates by Afghanistan are smuggled daily into Pakistan, an Afghan border official said.
- Seven people were killed in an armed clash between rival tribes in semi-autonomous tribal belt of Khyber and Orakzai agencies bordering Afghanistan.
